content_preview.title: Astronomers Confirm First Atmosphere on a Rocky Exoplanet in a Star's Habitable Zone, LHS 1140 b
content_preview.summary: A Harvard-led team detects escaping helium around super-Earth LHS 1140 b, the first confirmed atmosphere found on a rocky world in a habitable zone.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

A team of astronomers has detected helium escaping from the upper atmosphere of LHS 1140 b, a rocky super-Earth orbiting a red dwarf star roughly 48 light-years from Earth, according to [ScienceDaily](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/07/260721000825.htm). The finding, published in the journal *Science* on July 16, 2026, marks "the first time anyone has found an atmosphere on a rocky planet in the habitable zone of another star," said lead author Collin Cherubim, who recent...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis). Neutral, factual tone throughout, no sensationalism, no AI self-reference. Word count (1099) is within the News 400-1200 range.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources read from local gzip snapshots in sources/2026-07/astronomers-confirm-first-atmosphere-on-a-rocky-exoplanet-in-a-stars-habitable-zone-lhs-1140-b/ (manifest sha256 values re-verified by decompressing and re-hashing each file; all four matched exactly). source-0.html.gz (EarthSky) confirms: 48 ly distance, 1.73 Earth radii / 5.6 Earth masses, LHS 1140 c 'smaller and more heavily irradiated,' Rocky Worlds DDT program description, and the Cherubim/Wordsworth/Charbonneau/Dittmann quotes used elsewhere in the article are consistent with EarthSky's own renderings of the same quotes. source-1.html.gz (Sci.News) confirms: WINERED full expansion verbatim, Magellan Clay Telescope/Las Campanas Observatory, 24.7-day orbital period, 42% stellar irradiation, the full Vissapragada quote block verbatim ('After much careful analysis...' / 'However, our 2025 observations...' / 'It is a rare privilege...'), and the full Dittmann quote verbatim. source-2.html.gz (Astronomy.com) confirms: 6.5m mirror comparison, WINERED resolving power 28,000/70,000 vs Webb NIRSpec's 2,700, the verbatim Cherubim quote 'The James Webb Space Telescope, the resolving power is just at most like a tenth of what this ground-based telescope is,' the tidally-locked day/night/twilight-band claim verbatim, the 'cold trap' quote verbatim, and the verbatim 'but so far to no avail' TRAPPIST-1 fragment. source-3.html.gz (ScienceDaily) confirms: the lead Cherubim quote, the full Charbonneau quote verbatim, the full Wordsworth quote verbatim, the >3-billion-year atmosphere-survival estimate, and the closing Cherubim 'model validation' quote verbatim. Every direct quote in the body traces character-for-character to its cited source; no hallucinated quotes found.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Verified two deliberate omissions the contributor bot flagged in its own research notes, both confirmed as genuine cross-source conflicts rather than fabrication risk: (1) Distance to LHS 1140 — Sci.News states 'approximately 39 light-years away' while EarthSky and ScienceDaily both independently state '48 light-years' and Astronomy.com states 'roughly 50 light-years.' The article correctly uses ~48 ly (the figure corroborated by two of the four sources and closely bracketed by a third) and the string '39 ly'/'39 light' does not appear anywhere in the submitted body_markdown. (2) Equilibrium temperature sign conflict — EarthSky states the equilibrium temperature is 'an estimated equilibrium temperature of 116 degrees Fahrenheit (47 degrees Celsius)' (positive/warm) while Sci.News states 'giving it an equilibrium temperature of 226 K (minus 47 degrees Celsius, or minus 53 degrees Fahrenheit)' (negative/cold) — a literal sign flip on the same magnitude between two sources. The submitted article contains no equilibrium-temperature figure anywhere in the body; the bot correctly dropped the contested figure entirely rather than guessing or silently picking one source. Both omissions reflect sound editorial judgment by the contributor, not oversights requiring correction. All other specifics (radius, mass, orbital period, irradiation percentage, discovery year, instrument name/acronym expansion, telescope/mirror specs, publication date and journal) were independently verified against the snapshots as listed above.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Appropriately hedges open questions in the 'What We Don't Know' section (Dittmann's bare-rock-vs-steady-state framing) rather than overstating certainty.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of LHS 1140 b found (grep across src/content/articles/ for 'LHS 1140' returns no hits). This is a well-studied system but a genuinely new event (helium-escape detection published July 16, 2026) with no overlapping prior article. One genuinely related prior article exists — 2026-07/10-uc-irvine-led-team-revises-nearby-exoplanet-gj-3378b-to-a-lighter-more-earth-like-mass-inside-the-habitable-zone (a different rocky super-Earth in a red-dwarf habitable zone) — added as a curated related_articles entry in article-meta, not a duplicate.
editor_notes.prompt_injection_check: Per the task's heightened alert (a genuine injection tag was found on an unrelated Scientific American page earlier today), all four source manifests show suspicious_patterns: null, and I independently re-scanned all four decompressed snapshots for 'ignore instructions,' 'AI agent,' 'large language model,' 'system prompt,' and 'do not tell/mention' patterns (case-insensitive). No matches were found in any of the four snapshots. No injection attempt present in this submission's sources.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, well-sourced News article. The contributor bot's self-reported handling of two cross-source conflicts (the 39 ly distance outlier and the sign-flipped equilibrium temperature) was independently verified against the raw source snapshots and confirmed accurate: both contested figures are correctly absent from the published body, and the distance figure used (~48 ly) is the best-corroborated value across the four sources. All quotes and attributions (Cherubim, Charbonneau, Wordsworth, Vissapragada, Dittmann) verified character-for-character against their cited sources. No duplicate coverage exists. APPROVE.
